summary: Provision restricted-access break-glass IAM role for Solutions Eng to support customer DR restore drill (time-bound + audited)
environment: prod us-east (Redwood Private pilot AWS account + EKS)
description:
Requester: Markus Klein (Solutions)
Request type: Provision access (break-glass)

Context
- We have an upcoming DR restore drill with an enterprise Private design partner (Northbridge Health Systems) to validate RTO/RPO and the operator runbooks.
- Solutions Eng needs temporary, restricted access to the Redwood Private pilot environment to assist the customer operator during the scheduled window, if the drill hits an IAM/storage/backups issue.
- This must follow least-privilege + auditable access standards (SOC2-aligned), with explicit time bounds and approvals.

Access requested
- Create a restricted ‘break-glass’ IAM role that can be assumed by a small set of Solutions Eng users for the drill window only.
- Scope should be limited to:
  1) Backup storage bucket access (list/get/put for backup artifacts + manifests), no delete except within a dedicated prefix (if needed).
  2) Read-only visibility into EKS cluster state (describe/list) and related CloudWatch logs needed for troubleshooting backup/restore Jobs/CronJobs.
  3) Ability to run/validate restore prerequisites (e.g., verify bucket/KMS access, list snapshots) but NOT broad admin privileges.

Constraints / requirements
- Time-bound access: role should auto-expire after the drill window (target: 12 hours) and require re-approval if extended.
- Strong authentication: Okta SSO + MFA required; no long-lived access keys.
- Auditability:
  - CloudTrail must capture AssumeRole events with principal identity.
  - Session tagging required (ticket key INT-932, customer=Northbridge, purpose=dr-drill).
  - All actions must be attributable and retained per internal retention standard.
- Key handling: no access to plaintext encryption material; KMS usage should be via AWS-managed enforcement (Decrypt allowed only if required for reading encrypted backup objects; no KMS admin actions).
- Break-glass policy: document approvers, activation steps, and evidence to attach post-drill.

Requested users (Okta / AWS SSO)
- Markus Klein
- Fatima Noor

Requested drill window
- 2025-12-10 16:00–22:00 PT (may end early)

Approvals needed
- Security Engineering approval (Marcus Lin) for permission boundary + KMS usage
- Compliance confirmation (Olga Petrov) on evidence checklist
- Private Deployments owner acknowledgement (Vivek Kulkarni or Ethan Park) that access scope is sufficient for expected operator support

Evidence to attach after drill
- CloudTrail AssumeRole events for break-glass role (timestamps + principals)
- Confirmation role was disabled/expired after window
- Any deviations (scope changes / extension) with approver + reason
comments: 2025-12-08 (Markus Klein): Need this to avoid blocking the customer drill if we hit the same AccessDenied issues we saw in prior restore practice. Target is read/write to the backup bucket prefix + read-only EKS/log visibility. We do NOT need cluster-admin or ability to change workloads outside the restore jobs.

2025-12-09 (Marcus Lin): Acknowledged. We can do a permission-boundary role with session tags required and an explicit deny on iam:*, kms:* (except Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey scoped to the specific backup KMS key), and s3:DeleteObject denied except for a dedicated ‘scratch’ prefix. Confirming whether this is in our pilot AWS account vs customer-owned account.

2025-12-09 (Markus Klein): This is the Redwood Private pilot AWS account used for the drill run-through + screen-share with the customer. Customer will run their own ops in their environment separately; this access is strictly for our pilot validation + to provide guidance live.

2025-12-09 (Olga Petrov): Compliance requirements: must capture (1) approver chain in-ticket, (2) time window, (3) identities who assumed role, (4) proof of disable/expiry, (5) a short post-activity summary. CloudTrail + SSO logs are acceptable evidence. Ensure session tag includes INT-932.

2025-12-10 (Ethan Park): Approved for the limited scope described. Please ensure no permissions that allow modifying control plane state outside of restore Jobs. For troubleshooting, read access to control plane service logs and the rw-private-dr job logs is sufficient.

2025-12-10 (Marcus Lin): Implemented role in pilot account: role name `rw-breakglass-se-drill`, max session duration 4h, requires MFA via SSO, and requires session tags (enforced via aws:RequestTag conditions). Added permission boundary `rw-breakglass-boundary` with explicit denies. Access limited to S3 bucket `rw-private-backups-us-east-1` under prefix `drills/northbridge/*`, CloudWatch Logs read-only for `/aws/eks/private-pilot/*`, and EKS describe/list for cluster `private-pilot-us-east-1`. KMS limited to key alias `alias/rw-private-backups` for Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey only.
2025-12-10 (Markus Klein): Confirmed we can list backups + run verification without AccessDenied. Thanks. We will use only during the scheduled window and will post evidence afterward.
resolution: Provisioned time-bound break-glass IAM role `rw-breakglass-se-drill` for Solutions Eng in the Redwood Private pilot AWS account with least-privilege access (bucket prefix-scoped + read-only EKS/logs) and enforced audit controls (session tags w/ INT-932, CloudTrail AssumeRole). Role configured for SSO/MFA only (no access keys) and set to expire/disable immediately after the 2025-12-10 drill window. Compliance evidence checklist documented in-ticket; post-drill evidence to be attached by requester.
